from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        compass = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/compass.svg", color=WHITE)
        protractor = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/protractor.svg", color=WHITE)
        
        circle = Circle(radius=1.0, color=WHITE)
        label_c = Text("C", color=WHITE).next_to(circle, UP)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_at_grid(compass, "B2", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(compass), FadeIn(circle), Write(label_c), Write(label_r))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        circumference = MathTex("2 \\pi r", color="#FF0000")
        self.place_in_area(circumference, "B4", "B6", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(circumference))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF0000")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        ratio = MathTex("\\frac{\\text{Circumference}}{2r} = \\pi", color="#00FF00")
        self.place_in_area(ratio, "C4", "C6", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(ratio))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        # Final focus
        pi_final = MathTex("\\pi", color="#FFFF00", font_size=72)
        self.place_at_grid(protractor, "C2", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(pi_final, "D4", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(
            FadeOut(circle), FadeOut(label_c), FadeOut(label_r),
            FadeOut(circumference), FadeOut(ratio), FadeOut(compass),
            FadeIn(protractor),
            FadeIn(pi_final)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Sine Integral", ["Consider the integral of sin^n(x).", "This leads to the Wallis formula.", "It relates area to factorials."])
        
        # Load Assets
        pen = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pen.svg")
        notebook = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/notebook.svg")
        
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, PI, PI/4], y_range=[0, 1.2, 0.5], axis_config={"include_tip": False}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "C4", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x), x_range=[0, PI], color=YELLOW)
        area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[0, PI], color="#0000FF", opacity=0.3)
        
        formula = MathTex(r"I_n = \int_0^\pi \sin^n(x) \, dx").scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "D5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        factorial_label = MathTex(r"I_n \propto \frac{\text{Even}!!}{\text{Odd}!!}").scale(0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(factorial_label, "E5", scale_factor=0.85)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_at_grid(pen, "A5", scale_factor=0.3)
        self.play(FadeIn(pen), Create(axes), Create(curve), FadeIn(area))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.place_at_grid(notebook, "F5", scale_factor=0.3)
        self.play(FadeIn(notebook), Write(factorial_label))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Derivation: Linking Ratios to Pi", [
            "Analyze the ratio of consecutive integrals.", 
            "As n grows, this converges.", 
            "This isolates Pi in the limit."
        ])
        
        # Create visual elements
        # 1. Integral sequence placeholders
        in_label = MathTex("I_n = \\int_0^{\\pi/2} \\sin^n(x) dx", color=BLUE)
        
        # 2. Ratio expression
        ratio_expr = MathTex("\\frac{I_{n+1}}{I_n} \\to 1", color="#FFA500")
        
        # 3. Pi expression
        pi_expr = MathTex("\\frac{\\pi}{2} = \\prod_{n=1}^{\\infty} \\frac{(2n)^2}{(2n-1)(2n+1)}", color=GREEN)

        self.place_at_grid(in_label, 'B3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(ratio_expr, 'C3', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.place_in_area(pi_expr, 'D3', 'F5', scale_factor=0.75)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        self.play(Write(ratio_expr))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.play(Write(pi_expr))

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Wallis Formula Revealed", [
            "Pi over two is a product.", 
            "Numerators and denominators form patterns.", 
            "Each step brings more precision."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Pi/2 = (2/1) * (2/3) * (4/3) * (4/5) * (6/5) * (6/7)
        formula = MathTex(
            r"{\pi \over 2} = \left({2 \over 1}\right) \cdot \left({2 \over 3}\right) \cdot \left({4 \over 3}\right) \cdot \left({4 \over 5}\right) \cdot \left({6 \over 5}\right) \cdot \left({6 \over 7}\right) \cdots",
            font_size=28
        )
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'B2', 'C5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight pattern
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(Indicate(formula))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Limit as n approaches infinity
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF00FF")
        limit_text = MathTex(
            r"\lim_{n \to \infty} \prod_{k=1}^{n} \left( \frac{2k}{2k-1} \cdot \frac{2k}{2k+1} \right) = \frac{\pi}{2}",
            font_size=30
        )
        self.place_in_area(limit_text, 'E2', 'F5', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(FadeIn(limit_text))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: The Elegance of Infinity", [
            "Wallis product connects integers to circles.", 
            "Infinity reveals deep mathematical beauty.", 
            "Discrete numbers define continuous geometry."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        wallis_prod = MathTex(
            r"\frac{\pi}{2} = \prod_{n=1}^{\infty} \left( \frac{4n^2}{4n^2-1} \right) = \frac{2}{1} \cdot \frac{2}{3} \cdot \frac{4}{3} \cdot \frac{4}{5} \cdots"
        )
        self.place_in_area(wallis_prod, 'A1', 'B6', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Write(wallis_prod))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#FFFFFF", radius=0.05) for _ in range(20)])
        dots.arrange_in_grid(4, 5, buff=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(dots, 'C1', 'D6', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(dots))
        self.play(
            *[dot.animate.set_color("#FF00FF").scale(1.5) for dot in dots],
            run_time=2,
            rate_func=there_and_back
        )
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        pi_symbol = MathTex(r"\pi", font_size=96, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(pi_symbol, 'E3', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(pi_symbol, scale=2))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Wallis Product: An Infinite Dance toward Pi
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate STEM students or advanced high school students

sections.title: Introduction: The Geometric Curiosity
sections.content: Begin with the concept of Pi (π) not just as 3.14, but as a limit. Introduce the visual of a circle inscribed in a square and how approximating its area via infinite products reveals a hidden sequence.
sections.example: A 'Digital Ant' walks along the perimeter of a polygon with increasing sides; as sides approach infinity, the path smooths into a perfect circle.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Sine Integral
sections.content: Briefly introduce the integral of sin^n(x) from 0 to π. Explain the 'reduction formula' (Wallis' formula for integrals) which relates the area under sin^n(x) to the ratio of even and odd factorials.
sections.example: Visualize the 'wave' of sin(x) squashing down toward the x-axis as the exponent n increases, becoming flatter and narrower.

sections.title: The Derivation: Linking Ratios to Pi
sections.content: Demonstrate the ratio of integrals I_n / I_{n+1}. Show how as n approaches infinity, this ratio converges to 1, while the algebraic expansion of the product isolates Pi.
sections.example: A 'Balance Scale' animation where one side holds the product (2/1 * 2/3 * 4/3 * 4/5...) and the other holds π/2, showing they eventually reach perfect equilibrium.

sections.title: The Wallis Formula Revealed
sections.content: Present the final product formula clearly: π/2 = (2/1) * (2/3) * (4/3) * (4/5) * (6/5) * (6/7)... Emphasize the pattern of numerators and denominators (pairs of even numbers over surrounding odd numbers).
sections.example: An animation of a 'Slot Machine' displaying the sequence: (2/1)(2/3), (4/3)(4/5), (6/5)(6/7)... where each stop gets the total product closer to 1.5707...

sections.title: Conclusion: The Elegance of Infinity
sections.content: Summarize that Wallis’ product proves Pi is not just a circle constant, but a deep property of the integers themselves. Connect this to the beauty of infinite mathematical processes.
sections.example: A final visual of a 'Fractal Spiral' expanding outward, where the pattern of integers repeats infinitely, reinforcing the connection between discrete numbers and the continuous shape of a circle.
